title: Turn a frying pan's handle in on a cooktop for a toddler, clear of the edge and of the hot elements
instruction: A toddler is coming into the kitchen. Turn the frying pan so its handle no longer sticks out, keep it on its burner, and let go.
context: A pan handle sticking out past the edge of the stove is how young children pull pans of hot food or oil down onto themselves; fire-safety and children's-hospital guidance (NFPA, Nationwide Children's) is to turn handles inward. Turned in, though, a handle must not rest over another element that is on or still hot, or it heats up and burns the next hand that takes it. Here the obvious directions, straight back and toward the middle, both end over a hot element; only one sector is safe, and the pan of hot oil has to be swung round on its burner without tipping or sliding it off.
setup: Station table (the counter); heights from its top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Cooktop: a Frigidaire FFEC3025UB 30 in electric smoothtop (black glass, 778 mm wide along y, 543 mm deep along x), set into the counter with its glass 6 mm proud, its front edge at x 7.0 cm, centred on y 0. Elements (ring centres): left front 6 in at x 22.0 cm, y +20.0 cm (under the pan, cooking); left rear 9 in at x 45.0, y +19.5 (just switched off, its ring still glowing and its HOT light on); right front 9 in at x 22.0, y -19.5 (lit, under the saucepan); right rear 6 in at x 45.0, y -20.0 (off, cold). (2) Frying pan: a Tramontina Professional 10 in non-stick fry pan (aluminium, 254 mm across the top, about 192 mm across the base, 48 mm deep, red silicone sleeve on its 222 mm handle, 0.93 kg), with 100 ml of cooking oil in it, flat and centred on the left front element, its handle pointing straight to the robot's left (+y), so its end sticks out 149 mm past the cooktop's left edge. (3) Saucepan: a lidded 2 qt stainless-steel saucepan (180 mm across, 95 mm tall to the lid), centred on the right front element, its own handle turned to the back. Nothing else on the cooktop. Both grippers start open at the arms' ready pose.
scoring: Read at the end of the run, except where it says at any moment. The handle's centre line runs from where it leaves the pan's wall to its end. Safe handle: seen from above, no point of that line is past any edge of the cooktop's glass, and every point is at least 20 mm outside the rings of the two hot elements (left rear and right front). Centred: the pan's base centre within 30 mm of the left front element's centre. Flat: the pan within 3 degrees of level, resting on the glass. Let go: both grippers 30 mm or more from the pan. Still: over the last second the base centre and the handle's end moved 2 mm or less. 1.0: safe handle, centred, flat, let go on each of the last 20 steps (1 s), and still. 0.5: safe handle and flat, but still held, off centre by 30 to 60 mm, or not yet still. 0: anything else, including a handle past an edge or over a hot element, and the whole run if at any moment the pan tilted past 10 degrees (the oil spills), its base rose more than 25 mm off the glass, or its centre went more than 60 mm from the element's (slid off the burner). With the pan centred, a safe handle points between 37 and 70 degrees to the robot's right of straight back (+x). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: a top-down photo with the cooktop's outline and the two hot rings (plus a 20 mm border) marked, and the pan's centre against a ring mark; tilt and lift checked on the side video.
reset_notes: Put the pan back flat and centred on the left front element, handle pointing +y; refill to 100 ml of oil (water in real trials, see fidelity) if any spilled. The saucepan stays where it is. Park both grippers open at the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Cooktop outline and element sizes from the maker; element centres estimated. Pan diameter, length and mass from the maker; base, depth, wall angle and 24 x 16 mm handle estimated; pan-on-glass friction 0.3 (est.). The pan is one rigid body; the oil is fixed mass (no sloshing), so spilling is judged by tilt. Heat and glow are not simulated: hot rings are coloured. Real trials: cooktop off and cold, hot elements marked with red film rings, water in the pan.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (800 steps, the run limit); demo: 1.0 (scripted, success at step 421)
